title: Atomic Insights into Ferroelectric Properties in Moiré Superlattices
content: When stacked together, two-dimensional (2D) materials and related Van der Waals (VdW) heterostructures present a new paradigm for exploring exotic physical properties. Due to the lattice mismatch, neighboring crystal layers could undergo lattice reconstruction that breaks the inversion symmetry. Such local structural variations promote charge redistribution between crystal layers and create strong geometrical confinement to potential field, which, in turn, lead to the emergent ferroelectric order in moiré superlattices [1,2]. For instance, a marginal twist between the 2D lattices of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) or other VdW materials lead to interlayer charge transfer via hybridization between the occupied states of one layer and the unoccupied states of its neighbor. This mechanism gives rise to out-of-plane electric polarization, with polarization reversal achievable through lateral sliding under an applied electric field [3]. While the out-of-plane polarization mechanism is well established in moiré superlattices, the in-plane polarization component—induced by interlayer translations within stacking domains—remains insufficiently explored, a gap that has sparked growing interest due to its potential impact on electronic properties [1,4].
